exposure: Average heart rate at 90-120 seconds after birth
Average heart rate at 90-120 s after birth
outcome: Neonatal unit admission for respiratory distress
cohort: 298 at-risk infants born at ≥35 weeks gestation with a paediatric doctor in attendance who were initially vigorous and received delayed cord clamping for >60 seconds
finding: Risk factors independently associated with delivery room respiratory support were average heart rate (HR) at 90-120 s after birth (determined using three-lead ECG), mode of birth and time to establish regular cries.
mod_finding: Infants at highest risk of needing delivery room respiratory support had an average HR of <165 beats per minute at 90-120 s after birth following caesarean section (risk of 39%).
